transcript.text: dishwaher leakin water all over the floor and the plug sockets are right next to it whats going on

Water near the plug or socket is dangerous. Please don't touch the plug, socket or machine if they or your hands are wet. If you can do it safely, switch off the circuit at the consumer unit (fuse box), keep away from the water, and don't use the machine again until a qualified electrician or appliance engineer has checked it. Because water is leaking onto the floor right next to plug sockets, this is an immediate electrical safety risk. Do not use it again until a qualified engineer has checked it. Regarding what might be causing the leak: common causes include a damaged door seal, items in the racks deflecting water out of the door, or an internal leak that has triggered the anti-flood switch. To help narrow this down safely (with the power off), please check if there is anything caught in the rubber door seal or if tall trays are blocking the spray arms. Also, look underneath the machine to see if water is pooling inside the base tray.
its still running tho!! theres loads of bubbles coming out the door and the water is spreading toward an extension lead on the floor. should i just turn it off at the wall??

Do not reach for the plug if your hands are wet or if you have to stand in water; switch off the circuit breaker (fuse) instead. The bubbles suggest you may have used hand washing-up liquid by mistake, which creates massive foam that forces water out of the door. However, because this water is spreading towards an extension lead and plug sockets, there is a serious risk of electric shock or fire. Please do not use the machine again until a qualified engineer has checked both the leak source and the electrical safety.
yeah my housemate squirted fairy washing up liquid in cos we ran out of tablets. i dont know where the fuse box is tho, is it ok to just turn it off at the wall socket?

Yes, it is safe to turn off the power at the wall socket (the plug) if you cannot find the fuse box, provided your hands are dry and you do not have to stand in water to reach it. If you feel any doubt or see sparks, go straight to the consumer unit (fuse box) instead. The bubbles confirm that using Fairy washing-up liquid has created a massive amount of foam, which is forcing water out of the door. Because this water is spreading towards an extension lead and plug sockets, there is a serious risk of electric shock or fire. Please do not use the machine again until a qualified engineer has checked both the leak source and the electrical safety. Once you have switched off the power safely, please check if anything is caught in the rubber door seal or if tall items are blocking the spray arms. Also look underneath to see if water has pooled in the base tray.
ok ill turn it off at the wall, my hands are dry. then what do i do about all the water and foam?

To deal with the mess: do not try to run the machine again to 'wash it out'—the foam will just get worse and spread more water. 1. Contain the water: Use old towels or rags to soak up the standing water on the floor, especially near the extension lead and sockets. If you have a wet/dry vacuum (domestic vacuum), use that to suck up the bulk of the water and foam from the floor.
2. The pressure may be holding it shut; if so, wait a moment or pull firmly but gently. Use cups or bowls to scoop out as much of the soapy foam as you can into a bucket (do not pour this down the sink yet, as it will overflow). Wipe the inside with towels.
3. Do not use again: Because water is on the floor near electrical points, do not plug the machine back in or try to run any cycles. You need a qualified engineer to check for electrical damage and to help you drain the remaining foam safely.
